liveIntegration: earlier eleven registered locally; final three await separate-module receipts
reviewScope: All fourteen chapter-eight coding exercises and seventy actual language bodies reviewed. No chapter-eight exercise is replaced by a merely similar task.

questions.algorithm: Iterate the three-term last-hop recurrence while retaining only the three preceding counts.
questions.review: Counts ordered hop sequences, including the empty route for zero. Negative signed inputs return zero before a loop or allocation. Every steps value through 36 is executed, including the largest signed-safe result 2082876103. No two-hop staircase function is substituted.
questions.complexity: O(steps) time for nonnegative inputs and O(1) space match every rolling-state implementation; no recursive stack or memo array is claimed.

questions.algorithm: Row-order predecessor DP followed by reverse path reconstruction.
questions.review: The author Java source establishes a single right/down path, unlike the public community all-path variant. Grid cells use explicit 0/1 wire values. All five bodies preserve input outer/row identities and cells; any legal path is accepted independently of the oracle path. Empty/blocked endpoints, all 3x3 obstacle grids, larger grids and right/down-only restrictions are covered. Concrete List/vector coordinates and O(rows*columns) tables match the explanations.

questions.algorithm: Iterative binary search for the distinct promise; duplicate-aware bounded recursive search otherwise.
questions.review: Every implementation compares values directly with middle indices without subtracting signed endpoints. Duplicate recursion bounds each half using the middle value, and any valid index is accepted rather than demanding the oracle first match. Both flags, empty arrays, multiple answers, signed endpoints and 10000-element boundaries are executed. Distinct input has O(log n) work and O(1) storage; duplicates have O(n) worst-case work and O(log n) stack.

questions.algorithm: Iteratively double the subset collection by appending independent copies with the next distinct member.
questions.review: All languages snapshot the previous subset count, copy each old subset, and preserve the caller input. Both outer ordering and within-subset order are accepted by the independent property grader. Duplicate subsets and duplicate members fail; empty input produces one empty subset. Python mutation observation distinguishes an integer from an equal-valued bool.

questions.algorithm: Recursively multiply the halved smaller operand once, double that partial result by addition, and add the larger operand for an odd smaller operand.
questions.review: All five actual bodies use no multiplication or division operation. Their recursive call reduces the smaller operand and computes one half only. Zero, odd/even values, swapped arguments, every pair 0..31 and the maximum product are covered. Every intermediate sum stays within the admitted exact signed result range.

questions.algorithm: Recursively transfer a canonical initial three-stack puzzle, performing actual top pops/pushes and recording [disk,source,destination].
questions.review: Every language initializes three private stacks, with end-of-list or actual Stack/Deque tops. Recursive role permutation exposes the largest disk before moving it and transfers smaller disks afterward. An independent iterative legal-move cycle supplies expected ordered moves; a separate simulation checks every pop, size rule, final state and 2^n-1 bound through twelve disks. C# Stack and Java Deque use their documented top; Python/JS/C++ list/vector back is the top. Transcript output replaces public printing, not the tower-transfer task.

questions.algorithm: Swap each remaining character into the next fixed position, recurse, then restore the swap.
questions.review: The ASCII/distinct-character domain makes branches disjoint. Every emitted string copies the current character buffer. The empty permutation and all 40320 outputs at length eight are executed; no sorted output order is required.

questions.algorithm: Backtrack by remaining letter frequencies rather than by equal input occurrences.
questions.review: Every language decrements before descent and restores afterward, with a fresh length-n buffer and 26 counters per call. Equal copies never form separate branches. Multiplicities, all-equal input, all-distinct input and empty input are covered, and duplicate returned strings fail.

questions.algorithm: Backtrack only valid prefixes using opened/closed counts.
questions.review: Opening is bounded by the requested pair count, and closing is permitted only when it matches an unmatched opening. Complete buffers are copied to returned strings. All pair counts zero through eight are executed and checked against an independent arbitrary-string enumeration oracle, including all 1430 outputs for eight pairs.

questions.algorithm: Iterative work-stack flood fill, recoloring matching cells when discovered before enqueueing.
questions.review: The author Java source uses four neighbors; the community eight-neighbor version is explicitly excluded. Bank conventions define integer colors, returned filled values and graceful invalid-coordinate no-ops. Every language preserves original outer and row objects while changing exactly component cells. Same-color early return avoids revisiting forever. C++ takes a mutable reference and returns a value copy, with copy time/space stated; other languages return the existing screen. Independent component discovery precedes recoloring in the oracle. Exhaustive binary 3x3 screens and diagonal-only cases expose eight-neighbor mistakes.

questions.algorithm: Denomination-first one-dimensional combination DP, increasing amounts within each denomination pass.
questions.review: The fixed denominations are 1,5,10,25 cents. Empty amount counts once. The loop nesting counts unordered combinations with unlimited reuse, not sequences or minimum coins. The independent oracle enumerates quarter and dime counts and directly counts feasible nickel/penny choices. The admitted maximum is executed in all five languages.
questions.complexity: O(4*amount) time and O(amount) storage match the actual DP arrays. Counts are exact, not reduced modulo another number.

questions.algorithm: Row backtracking with occupied column and two diagonal masks; copy completed eight-column boards.
questions.review: All five bodies create fresh state each call and append copies only at row eight. C# List, Java ArrayList, C++ vector, Python list.copy and JS slice prevent shared-buffer corruption. The independent permutation/diagonal oracle has 92 answers. Only outer board order is ignored; inner column order encodes rows, and symmetry representatives do not suffice. Three repeated calls execute against the full collection.

questions.algorithm: Sort auxiliary indices by width; compute the best height with each indexed box as bottom by checking all earlier strictly smaller boxes.
questions.review: All three dimensions use strict inequalities; height is always dimension one and rotation is never permitted. The input outer array, row references, contents and order are observed unchanged. Sorting index objects or integers changes no boxes. The independent oracle exhausts strictly fitting paths without sorted DP. O(n^2) pair checks and O(n) arrays match each implementation.

questions.algorithm: Bottom-up interval tables count true and false full binary groupings via each outer operator split.
questions.review: All five languages use increasing interval lengths and the same Boolean truth tables, not operator precedence. Empty input returns zero; the desired flag selects one complete-interval count. Independent enumeration returns an evaluation for every binary grouping and covers all expressions through four literals plus maximum 13-literal chains with Catalan(12)=208012. C# rectangular and other-language nested tables remain independent; all integer products and sums stay within the admitted total grouping bound.

languageBindingReview.csharp: Signed int bounds are justified by the explicit domains and executed endpoints. Arrays are zero-initialized, ways[0] is set before the denomination passes, and recursive multiplication uses ordinary method self-calls without hidden helper state. Collection outputs use concrete Lists. Local recursive functions copy char buffers into immutable strings; the set grader canonicalizes member/outer ordering and rejects boolean or oversized integer members without an exception.
languageBindingReview.javascript: All results and intermediate sums stay below signed 32-bit maximum and therefore are exact Numbers. The smaller multiplication operand is below 2^16, making its unsigned right shift well-defined for this domain. Each call creates its own DP array. Destructuring swaps restore the exact original character order before siblings. Returned values are real Arrays; input mutation checks use strict scalar equality. Frequency counts and parentheses counters remain local to each invocation.
languageBindingReview.python: The recursive function's module-global name refers to itself even when invoked through the exported adapter alias. Rolling assignment evaluates previous values before rebinding. Arbitrary-size ints do not mask another language's overflow because shared admitted bounds are verified. Subsets and string collections must be concrete lists. Input snapshot checks require exact int elements, catching bool substitution despite Python equality. Every returned string is joined from the full buffer at a leaf.
languageBindingReview.cpp: vector<int> zero-initializes the coin counts; std::array enumerates the four denominations. The recursive method calls itself on a strictly smaller nonnegative operand, and all signed additions remain in range. Primitive parameters are passed by value. const references protect scalar-array and string inputs. std::function recursion captures local buffers/results by reference and is invoked only while they live. Subset copies are moved into the result after construction; outer-vector growth does not invalidate an in-use source reference.
languageBindingReview.java: int arithmetic is exact within the admitted count/product bounds. The recurrence and coin arrays are local to each invocation; no static cached result leaks across tests. Recursive multiplication calls the same instance method with reduced arguments. Local Search classes capture effectively-final buffer/result references. Mutation of array contents is intentional workspace use, while each output string is copied. Boxed integer subset values are encoded by value; input int arrays are compared against untouched snapshots.
